content: 1. Adjust the dosage of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as needed, as sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels or effects of etravirine by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Both trimethoprim and finerenone elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and serum potassium levels should be monitored closely. Adjust the finerenone dose based on current serum potassium concentrations as per prescribing information. 3. Sulfamethoxazole and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, flecainide and trimethoprim also increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor these combinations. 4. Fluconazole and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and fluconazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 5. Fluoxetine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Fluoxetine also increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Fluphenazine and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval, as do fluphenazine and sulfamethoxazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 7. Fluvoxamine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do fluvoxamine and sulfamethoxazole. Use caution and monitor. 8. Sulfamethoxazole and formoterol both increase the QTc interval, as do formoterol and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 9. Sulfamethoxazole and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval, as do foscarnet and trimethoprim. Use caution and monitor. 10. Trimethoprim and fosinopril both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially at high doses, in renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 11. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Conversely, fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Sulfamethoxazole increases glimepiride levels through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor. 13. Sulfamethoxazole increases glipizide levels via plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor. 14. Glucarpidase reduces the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by increasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Glucarpidase also decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by increasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 15. Sulfamethoxazole increases glyburide levels through plasma protein binding competition and by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may reduce glyburide metabolism. 16. Haloperidol and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do haloperidol and sulfamethoxazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 17. Sulfamethoxazole and iloperidone both increase the QTc interval, as do iloperidone and trimethoprim. Iloperidone also increases trimethoprim levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may elevate plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. 18. Imatinib increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Imipramine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do imipramine and sulfamethoxazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Trimethoprim and irbesartan both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially at high doses, in renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 22. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 23. Sulfamethoxazole and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval, as do itraconazole and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Ketoconazole and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and ketoconazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 25. Trimethoprim reduces the effects of L-methylfolate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Folic acid antagonists may interfere with folic acid utilization. 26. Sulfamethoxazole increases lacosamide levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 27. Trimethoprim increases the effects of lamivudine through cationic drug competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential increased toxicity. 28. Sulfamethoxazole and lapatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 29. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lenacapavir may elevate CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 30. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of lesinurad by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 31. Sulfamethoxazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, as do levofloxacin and trimethoprim. Use caution and monitor. 32. Levo-ketoconazole and trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval, as do sulfamethoxazole and levo-ketoconazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 33. Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Sulfamethoxazole has a similar effect. 34. Trimethoprim and lisinopril both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially at high doses, in renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 35. Lofepramine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval, as do lofepramine and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 36. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of losartan by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. This may inhibit the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite E-3174. Trimethoprim and losartan both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 37. Lumacaftor may induce, and ivacaftor may inhibit, CYP2C9 substrates. Use caution and monitor when coadministered with trimethoprim. 38. Sulfamethoxazole and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, as do lumefantrine and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 39. Maprotiline and sulfamethoxazole both increase the QTc interval, as do maprotiline and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 40. Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Sulfamethoxazole has a similar effect. 41. Trimethoprim increases metformin levels by inhibiting active renal tubular secretion (e.g., via OCT2, MATE1). Dose adjustments may be necessary. Use caution and monitor. 42. Sulfamethoxazole and methadone both prolong the QTc interval, as do methadone and trimethoprim. Use caution and monitor. 43. Trimethoprim increases the toxicity of methotrexate by raising the risk of bone marrow suppression and megaloblastic anemia. If this combination cannot be avoided, closely monitor for hematologic toxicity. 44. Sulfamethoxazole and methoxsalen both increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive photosensitizing effects. Use caution and monitor. 45. Sulfamethoxazole and metronidazole may cause a disulfiram-like reaction due to decreased metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Sulfamethoxazole and mipomersen both have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 47. Mitotane decreases trimethoprim levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 48. Trimethoprim and moexipril both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 49. Sulfamethoxazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, as do moxifloxacin and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 50. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of nateglinide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor. 51. Nitisinone increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor, particularly with CYP2C9 substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 52. Sulfamethoxazole and nilotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 53. Nortriptyline and sulfamethoxazole both increase the QTc interval, as do nortriptyline and trimethoprim. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 54. Octreotide and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do octreotide and sulfamethoxazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 55. Sulfamethoxazole and ofloxacin both increase the QTc interval, as do ofloxacin and trimethoprim. Use caution and monitor. 56. Trimethoprim and olmesartan both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 57. Sulfamethoxazole increases ospemifene levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 58. Trimethoprim increases paclitaxel levels/toxicity when coadministered with CYP2C8 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 59. Sulfamethoxazole and paliperidone both prolong the QTc interval, as do paliperidone and trimethoprim. Use caution and monitor. 60. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Paroxetine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do paroxetine and sulfamethoxazole. Use caution and monitor. 62. Trimethoprim and pentamidine both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 63. Trimethoprim and perindopril both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 64. Perphenazine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval, as do perphenazine and sulfamethoxazole. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 65. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of phenytoin by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Posaconazole and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 67. Sulfamethoxazole and porfimer both enhance photosensitivity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 68. Trimethoprim and potassium acid phosphate both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 69. Trimethoprim and potassium chloride both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor.
